item.title: MiBeeNvr: From v0.1.0 to v0.12.0
item.description: MiBeeNvr is an NVR built for a home camera fleet. v0.1.0 shipped on May 6, 2026; v0.12.0 on September 1 — twelve releases in a bit over four months. This post merges the per-release notes from v0.1.0 through v0.12.0 into one timeline: what each step did, and why. The house style for mechanisms is plain words first, then a picture, then the parameters. The v0.13.0 performance benchmarks are a separate post, linked at the end.

item.title: From H.265 to AV1 and AVS: Bitstream Structures Across Codec Standards, Plus Surveillance Smart Codecs
item.description:
The first two posts stayed inside H.264. This one covers the remaining mainstream standards in one pass: what each changed at the bitstream level and why, ending with surveillance-specific “smart codecs” (H.265+ / Smart Codec) — the layer responsible for the familiar “plays fine on the same brand, storage balloons across brands” effect when an NVR ingests third-party cameras.

Data caveats up front: compression figures are ranges from standards-body verification tests or public studies (JVET/JCT-VC official tests, MDPI comparisons, AVS workgroup claims) and vary with content and bitrate; smart-codec savings are vendor marketing figures and are labeled as such. Web playback selection conclusions are in the earlier post; this one only looks inside the bitstream.

item.title: H.264 / H.265 / H.266 Web Frontend Playback: Which Generation to Pick in 2026
item.description: The previous post traced bitstream structures from H.265 through AV1/AVS; this one comes back to the browser: which generation should you actually use. In the MiBee NVR surveillance-dashboard project, should the frontend pull H.264 or H.265 from all 16 cameras? A seemingly simple question that gets deeper the more you dig. H.265 needs only half the bitrate of H.264 at the same quality, saving both bandwidth and storage. But plenty of online sources still claim “H.265 browser support is poor, Firefox doesn’t support it, you need to install extensions.” Which of these claims still hold?
